intro: Benevento's two registered giants share one city park, the Villa Comunale, about ten minutes' walk from the town centre. On the park's belvedere terrace a holm oak four and a half metres round spreads its limbs over the benches, the native evergreen oak of southern Italy at full width. About a hundred metres away a coast redwood from California rises to 33 metres, fifteen metres taller. Both are free to see in an open city park, and together they make a short walk.
meta_description: Benevento's monumental trees: a holm oak 4.55 m round on the Villa Comunale terrace and a coast redwood 33 m tall, a hundred metres apart.
question_meta: Benevento's most remarkable tree is a holm oak 4.55 metres round, spreading over the belvedere terrace of the Villa Comunale.
question_answer: Benevento's most remarkable tree is the holm oak of the Villa Comunale, 4.55 metres round and 18 metres tall on Italy's national register of monumental trees. It spreads in several great limbs over the benches of the park's belvedere terrace. Nobody has published its age, so which tree in the city is oldest remains an open question.
question_context: Both of Benevento's trees here come from Italy's national register of monumental trees, which records girth and height but no age, and neither has a published planting record. So the city's oldest tree cannot honestly be named. What can be said is which is biggest. The holm oak on the belvedere terrace of the Villa Comunale has the thickest trunk, 455 centimetres, and the register records no other holm oak that size in the park. A naturalist photographed it in July 2024, a wide, many-limbed tree with benches in its shade and a viewpoint rail beside it. The coast redwood, about a hundred metres away, wins on height at 33 metres against the oak's 18, and naturalists recorded redwoods in the park in 2021 and 2024. The two make a natural pair, a native evergreen oak that spreads sideways and an imported conifer that only goes up. The park is free and open air, about ten minutes on foot from the centre and about 1.5 km from the station. If you know when either tree was planted, tell us.

faq.q: What is the oldest tree in Benevento?
faq.a: Nobody has published a date for any of them. The biggest is the holm oak on the belvedere terrace of the Villa Comunale, 4.55 metres round, and if you know when it was planted, tell us.

Both stand in the Villa Comunale, the city park on Piazza IV Novembre, about ten minutes' walk from the town centre and about 1.5 km from the station. The holm oak is on the belvedere terrace and the redwood about a hundred metres away.

faq.q: Do you have to pay to see them?
faq.a: No. The Villa Comunale is a free, open-air city park.

trees.name: The Holm Oak of the Villa Comunale, Benevento

location.address: Villa Comunale, Piazza IV Novembre, 82100 Benevento

trees.story:
The best seat in Benevento's town park is under a holm oak four and a half metres round. Italy's national register of monumental trees lists it at 455 centimetres of girth and 18 metres tall, and it is the only holm oak that size the register records in the Villa Comunale.

The tree stands on the park's belvedere terrace, where benches sit under its crown and a rail marks the viewpoint. A naturalist photographed it there in July 2024, and the picture shows exactly why the register bothered. Instead of one trunk rising to a neat dome, it splits into several great limbs that spread wide over the terrace, so the shade reaches further than the height would suggest.

Holm oaks are the native evergreen oak of southern Italy, with small dark leaves that stay on through winter. That means this tree looks much the same in January as in August, and the shade on the terrace is there in every season.

Nobody has published an age for it, and there is no planting record for this tree in the park. The girth is the only clue, and girth alone is not a date. If you know when it was planted, tell us.

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 01/A783/BN/15

trees.access: Free. City park (Villa Comunale), open air; check opening hours before you go.
trees.transport: About 10 minutes' walk from Benevento town centre; the station is about 1.5 km away.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the very broad, many-limbed crown spreading over the benches on the park's belvedere terrace, beside the viewpoint rail.
trees.verify_notes: MASAF 455 cm, 18 m. Alive and placed: iNaturalist observation 2024-07-19 (Quercus ilex, cultivated, place Villa Comunale) at 41.127858,14.783887, about 15 m from the register point; the photo (viewed, not open licence) shows a huge, wide-spreading multi-limbed holm oak on a terrace with benches and a viewpoint rail, trunk visibly thick. The register sheet is the only 455 cm holm oak recorded in the park. Pin confirmed by that GPS fix at a tree that fits. No age source. Recognise: the very broad holm oak on the belvedere terrace with benches under its crown.

trees.name: The Coast Redwood of the Villa Comunale, Benevento

location.address: Villa Comunale, Piazza IV Novembre, 82100 Benevento

trees.story:
A coast redwood 33 metres tall grows in Benevento's town park, several thousand kilometres from the California fog belt where its species belongs. Italy's national register of monumental trees gives it that height and a trunk 3.5 metres round. That is fifteen metres taller than the park's great holm oak.

It stands in the Villa Comunale, about a hundred metres from that holm oak, a tree four and a half metres round on the belvedere terrace. The two make an easy pair, the native evergreen oak that spreads sideways and the imported conifer that only goes up.

Naturalists have recorded redwoods here in February 2021 and July 2024, a few dozen metres from the register point, so the tree is alive, though neither record pins the exact trunk. Look for the soft, fibrous reddish bark and the flat, feathery sprays of needles, and the height will do the rest.

Nobody has published when it was planted, and the register gives no age. If you know its story, tell us.

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 03/A783/BN/15

trees.transport: About 10 minutes' walk from the centre.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its height, a tall conifer with soft reddish bark and flat, feathery sprays of needles, about a hundred metres from the broad holm oak on the terrace.
trees.verify_notes: MASAF 350 cm, 33 m. iNaturalist observations of Sequoia sempervirens (cultivated) on 2021-02-05 at 41.128308,14.783000 (about 30 m away) and 2024-07-19 at 41.128998,14.782962 (about 48 m away); the 2024 photo shows only foliage. Alive; pin approximate. Recognise: the tallest conifer in the park, a feathery redwood with spongy red bark, about 100 m from the holm oak bnv_001.
